items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Sam, you know, we talked to brother, you see. [INTERVIEWEE] What did he play? We played, we played, we played, we played, we played, we played, we played tenor saxophone.

ctx.x: Yeah, right. See, he was playing with Sid and Desiree in a long time, he and my brother like Tom Johnson. But Tom's in California, too, a very good saxophone player. We had a saxophone, a clarinet player, was a very, very good, well, actually, if you've ever heard of it, by the name of Felix Goff. He used to play with Rizzly, when we were playing with Rizzly, old man Porter was playing who the former was, with Rizzly. And this boy named Felix Goff, he could play. Man, he could play some time. I thought, you know,…
Sam, you know, we talked to brother, you see.

What did he play? We played, we played, we played, we played, we played, we played, we played, we played tenor saxophone. And, we had to coach him to get up to take a course after he got the fright off him. He was tough, I'm telling you. And then he had McLaren, no time, no time, no time, I said a couple of months. He was sitting in the back of that plan and taking slow moves and things. Yeah, a couple of months. We had him at a bar on Brookhaven College, E.W. Brown. His daddy was over the Rabbitfoot Show one…
